relevant_files.rationale: Gateway is the orchestration entrypoint for route/plan/execute, checkpoint APIs, and desktop streaming endpoints.
Core plan-act engine with level templates, risk gate decisions, and checkpoint lifecycle.
Session lifecycle persistence for active/archived states, content routing, and snapshot indexing.
Canonical L1-L5 semantics, level configs, and routing rules used across APIs and UI payloads.
Desktop SSE client contract for /chat/stream, including terminal/decision/diagnostics handling.
Frontend orchestration state machine for streaming phases, fallback, and checkpoint recovery hints.
UI integration for quality decision display and checkpoint create/restore interactions.
Dependency container wires workflow/agent engines and startup prewarm behavior used by gateway.
Cross-domain workflow state contract for session metadata, decision fields, and loop controls.
Alternative checkpoint persistence/resume strategies relevant to long-running closure loops.
Session-level constraints define P0/P1/P2 closure scope and backward-compatible rollout requirements.

patterns.name: Gateway-centered orchestration
patterns.description: Gateway exposes both MCP tool mounts and REST endpoints, acting as the single integration hub for workflow, agents, and desktop app traffic.

patterns.name: Level semantics normalization
patterns.description: WorkflowLevel label/slug conversion normalizes L1-L5 across backend route/plan/stream payloads and frontend consumers.

patterns.name: Soft-gate first decision model
patterns.description: Workflow gate decisions and stream terminal payloads currently prioritize go/soft_go/no_go signaling before hard-blocking behavior.

patterns.name: Session filesystem as source of truth
patterns.description: SessionManager persists active/archived session state and route-based artifacts, enabling recoverability and auditability.

patterns.name: Dual checkpoint mechanisms
patterns.description: WorkflowEngine uses in-memory plus optional Git commit checkpoints, while resume_strategy persists checkpoint snapshots on disk; these need alignment for closure orchestration consistency.

patterns.name: Desktop stream-first UX with fallback
patterns.description: Desktop handles SSE content/progress/evaluation events and falls back to non-stream chat path when stream terminal is error/aborted.

patterns.name: Container-based lazy engine wiring
patterns.description: ServiceContainer provides lazy initialization and startup prewarm, reducing gateway cold-start and centralizing dependency composition.

integration_points.detail: workflow_route tool delegates to WorkflowEngine.route for level routing.
workflow_plan tool delegates to WorkflowEngine.plan for plan generation and template metadata.
workflow_execute tool delegates to WorkflowEngine.execute for step execution and gate response.
checkpoint_create endpoint bridges API calls to WorkflowEngine.create_checkpoint.
chat endpoint validates workflowLevel and routes requests through Commander + Writer orchestration path.
chat_stream endpoint provides desktop streaming contract with event types start/routing/progress/content/evaluation/done/error.
SSE terminal decision emits go/soft_go based on fallback diagnostics; error path emits no_go.
Gateway lifespan starts MCP services in parallel and prewarms container engines.
plan() auto-routes level, resolves template metadata, and materializes step dependencies.
execute() enforces dependency ordering, applies risk gate, and updates plan progress state.
create_checkpoint() supports optional git-based snapshot for rollback points.
init() creates session directories and session.json lifecycle metadata.
write() updates artifact files and appends snapshot index for traceability.
restore() moves archived session back to active and flips status.
WorkflowDecision defines machine-readable go/soft_go/no_go values used in gate contracts.
LevelRouter provides rule-based level routing used by engine/gateway decisions.
chatStream() consumes /chat/stream and parses SSE protocol into UI callbacks.
done event parser maps backend decision and terminal into StreamDonePayload.
runNormalChat() coordinates stream lifecycle, fallback to chat(), and checkpoint recovery messaging.
Evaluation panel invokes checkpoint create/restore endpoints for operator-controlled rollback.
workflow property lazily instantiates WorkflowEngine used by gateway tools and endpoints.

constraints: P0/P1/P2 closure must reuse existing gateway/workflow_engine/session_manager/desktop flow with minimal changes and backward compatibility.
Current gating is soft-first (decision signaling) and not a strict hard gate; hard enforcement should be introduced incrementally.
Checkpoint behavior is split between workflow_engine (in-memory + git optional) and resume_strategy (disk checkpoints), creating consistency risk for cross-session recovery.
Workflow route logic exists in multiple places (LevelRouter rules, WorkflowEngine keyword scoring, Commander route path), which can drift unless unified.
Streaming reliability depends on allowLlmFallback; when disabled and LLM unavailable, gateway returns hard error (503) before stream starts.
SessionManager defaults to .writing/sessions while workflow artifacts in current initiative are under .workflow/active; this implies path/model bridging requirements.
Desktop contract currently expects decision and diagnostics in done/error events; any gateway payload changes must preserve this shape.
Gateway startup relies on parallel MCP session startup + engine prewarm, so new orchestration modules must avoid blocking lifespan initialization.

clarification_needs.question: P0 closure should prioritize which source of truth for session persistence?
clarification_needs.context: Session state currently spans .writing/sessions (SessionManager) and .workflow/active (project workflow artifacts).
options: Keep dual storage and add mapping layer
Converge all workflow closure artifacts into .workflow

clarification_needs.question: When should hard gate be enabled for P1/P2?
clarification_needs.context: Existing design emits soft_go/no_go signals but does not block execution by default.
options: P1 keep soft gate only, P2 enable hard gate for selected high-risk routes
Enable hard gate immediately for all L3+ routes
Keep soft gate through P2 and defer hard gate to later release

clarification_needs.question: Which checkpoint mechanism should be canonical for rollback APIs?
clarification_needs.context: workflow_engine and resume_strategy maintain separate checkpoint stores and semantics.
options: Use workflow_engine as API canonical source and sync to resume_strategy
Use resume_strategy as canonical source and adapt gateway endpoints
Expose both explicitly via separate API namespaces

clarification_needs.question: How should workflow level routing be unified across gateway, engine, and commander?
clarification_needs.context: There are at least three routing paths that can diverge under edge prompts.
options: Centralize on LevelRouter and treat others as adapters
Centralize on Commander route and deprecate engine-level heuristics
Keep current multi-router setup with periodic contract tests

clarification_needs.question: Desktop streaming contract versioning needed for P2 semantics unification?
clarification_needs.context: Client consumes contract_version, terminal, decision, and diagnostics; schema evolution impacts backward compatibility.
options: Freeze current event schema and add additive fields only
Allow in-place breaking contract update with desktop lockstep
